name: Usability, user-story and style review of the whole addon, ranked and independently verified

context.prompt: Write the review as context/ux-review-2026-11-19.md for a developer with zero context: a short method line, then the verified findings table from the synthesis (id, area, lens, severity, title, where, evidence, suggestion, effort), marking each verifier verdict (confirmed / refuted / partly), then the user-story table per area (story, status works|friction|broken, evidence), then the proposed fix batches. Add one dated line to state.md (review done, no code changed, awaiting user choice of fixes) and a dated insights.md entry with the 3-5 most important cross-cutting patterns. Do not edit any code or test file.

nodes.prompt:
READ-ONLY UX REVIEW of one area of the World of Warcraft addon Quest Sharing. Repo /Users/cozzolif/Desktop/cutpdf (Lua 5.1 in QuestSharing/, Python+lupa harness in tests/). Your area: {{item.area}}. Main files: {{item.files}}. Related tests: {{item.tests}}. Read README.md (the user-facing description of your area), context/architecture.md and the code. The player base: classic-era WoW players who quest, often in a party; many are not technical.
Three lenses, all required:
(1) USER STORIES: write 4-8 concrete stories for your area ('As a <player>, I want <goal> so that <reason>'), then walk each one end to end in the harness (drive it like the existing tests do: Game(style, ...), g.start(), g.slash(...), g.fire(...), click frames, read the visible text) and mark it works / friction / broken with evidence (the exact text the player sees, number of steps or clicks, dead ends, missing feedback).
(2) USABILITY: discoverability (how does a player find it: slash command, settings tab, minimap, menu?), feedback after an action, error/empty states and their wording, consistency of names for the same thing across settings, tooltips, chat output and README, number of clicks, defaults, keyboard/Esc behaviour, combat restrictions explained.
(3) STYLE: does every window/row follow the classic WoW look in Style.lua (S.window/S.frame/S.panel/S.inset/S.button/S.checkBox, opaque stone, gold border, GameFont* templates) and tests/test_classic_style.py; readable sizes; colour meaning consistent (gold = selected/heading, grey = disabled); plain wording without jargon or developer terms (no 'provider', 'DB', 'job', 'slice'); chat message prefix and tone consistent.
Rules: do NOT modify any repository file (no edits, no git stash/checkout); scratch files only under /tmp/ux-review-<short area>/; do NOT run the whole test suite (other reviewers run in parallel) — only targeted probes and at most the related test files listed. Report only real findings with evidence (path:line and/or the exact visible text); no generic advice. Severity: high = a player cannot finish a story or is misled; medium = clear friction or inconsistency; low = polish. Effort S/M/L. Return one object: {area, stories:[...], findings:[...]}.

nodes.name: Rank and batch findings
nodes.prompt:
You receive five area reviews of the WoW addon Quest Sharing (repo /Users/cozzolif/Desktop/cutpdf): {{areas}}
Produce ONE ranked synthesis: (1) merge duplicates across areas (same root cause = one finding, list every 'where'); give each kept finding an id like UX-01, ordered high -> low severity, then by player impact; keep evidence and suggestion concrete; drop anything without evidence. (2) Keep the user-story tables (area, story, status, evidence). (3) Group the findings into 3-5 fix batches a builder could take one at a time (by file ownership so batches do not edit the same files), each with ids and a one-line why. (4) List 3-5 cross-cutting patterns (e.g. inconsistent naming, missing empty states). Read code only to confirm a merge; do not invent findings.

nodes.name: Verify top findings
nodes.prompt:
Independent check of a UX review of the WoW addon Quest Sharing (repo /Users/cozzolif/Desktop/cutpdf, Lua 5.1 in QuestSharing/, Python+lupa harness in tests/ run with /tmp/qs-test-env/bin/python from tests/). Ranked findings: {{synthesis.findings}}
For EVERY high-severity finding and at least the first 8 medium ones: try to REFUTE it. Re-read the cited code yourself and reproduce the visible behaviour in the harness (scratch scripts only under /tmp/ux-review-verify/). Verdict confirmed (reproduced as described), partly (real but smaller/different than claimed — say how) or refuted (not reproducible or already handled — show where). Do not modify repository files. Return {checked:[{id, verdict, evidence}], summary}.
